chapter: Decca records, the Savoy and Moe Gale
title: Battle with Lucky Millinder's band
summary: McShann held back for three sets, then the band went into its books and out-played Lucky Millinder's, who afterwards fired three men.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And so we went in with this particular night, whatever night it was, we opened up with Lucky's band and so I told the cats, I said, look, man, they tell me Lucky is one of the favorites around here. What I think we ought to do we'll just play it kind of cool. We'll play some stocks for about the first two sets, maybe three sets, because we'll just kind of lay low and whatever they do I said, we're not going to pay it too much attention, just let them go on and do what they're going to do.

But, I said, after that we're going to have -- I think we're going to start getting in the books, okay, we played the first set, Lucky come on and we played a second set and Lucky began to bristle up, you know -- we played a first set
and old Byrd just kept hollering, man, when you going to get in the books. Get in the books. Anyway, so after the third set, we started getting in the books.
Lucky I take it had been playing all his best flag wavers and everything.

You know, Lucky, he was quite a showman there was no question about it. He was doing all that stuff, you know what I mean, and the band, playing all them heavy tunes, you know, so after we started going in the books, starting setting them tempos, then the house begin doing this because everybody's going along with the music, so then Lucky, we used to go downstairs and drink, and he was down there at the place, taking a taste, so Lucky's valet went down there and told him, Lucky, you better come upstairs. He said you better come up and see what these guys are doing up here. What are you talking about, them western dogs? We... going to run them back to the sticks.

Well, I don't know, Lucky, I think you should come up here. I ain't worried about it. Well, Lucky came back up and he went into his books. So when he went into -- so he went down in his books, well, when he did that, then I think that's when we -- we went heavy in the books. And Lucky come back after we went heavy in the books, they clapped about 15 minutes of Lucky's time, so he only got a chance to play 15 minutes, because they clapped and stomped, when he got through

with that last tune, we fell right into him and that was one tune, that 30 minute tune, we played that 30 minute tune, we had the same reaction again, about 20 minutes they were just hollering and screaming for 20 minutes and Lucky couldn't go on.
What was the number you played.
That wasn't Mary Lou's Roll 'Em, was it.

No, no, that was our own Kansas City Roll 'Em and so that was it. And so then Lucky, he called me over, 'come here you old devil so and so' and he says, 'my God, listen,' he said 'I want you to go with me this morning,' and I said, 'okay, all right.' Well, Buchanan had been waiting, brought me up there once or twice for Lucky to meet. Lucky said I ain't got time, I'm leading the band. I'll catch you later on.

So Buchanan didn't have to bring me back because Lucky come over and got me and said you go with me this morning. He took me around the town and we had a few tastes, which was nice, but he told me, 'I'll tell you, man, you guys blew us out of there, did you know that?' I said, 'oh, no,' and he said, 'yes, yes, I got so carried away and excited and everything I fired three of my good men there.' He did fire three of them that night, of course, they knew he was going through that thing.
